_comment: CELPIP Listening Part 3: Listening for Information. One person explains something to another, heard once, then 6 questions.

items.title: A new job orientation
items.context: You will hear a conversation between a human resources coordinator and a new employee.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Welcome to Brightwave Foods, Omar. Before you start on the production floor, I just want to go over a few important things.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Sure, thanks.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: First, your schedule. For the first two weeks, you'll work the day shift, from seven a.m. to three p.m., so you can train with a supervisor. After that, you'll join the rotating schedule, which includes some evening shifts.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Okay. How will I know my schedule each week?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It's posted in the staff app every Thursday for the following week. If you want to switch a shift with a coworker, you can request it in the app, but your supervisor has to approve it at least forty-eight hours in advance.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Got it. What about breaks?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: You get a thirty-minute unpaid lunch break and two paid fifteen-minute breaks. The cafeteria on the second floor is open from six a.m. until midnight, and employees get a twenty percent discount.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Great. And I was told I'd need safety equipment?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes. We'll give you steel-toed boots, a hairnet and gloves today. The boots are free, but if you lose them, you'll have to pay for a new pair. Also, no jewellery is allowed on the production floor, not even watches.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Okay. When do I get paid?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Every second Friday, by direct deposit. Your first pay will be on the twenty-first. Oh, and one more thing: after three months, you'll be able to join our health benefits plan. I'll send you the form by email.

questions.prompt: What will Omar do during his first two weeks?
questions.explanation: He will work the day shift so he can train with a supervisor.

questions.prompt: When is the work schedule posted?
questions.explanation: 'It's posted in the staff app every Thursday.'

questions.prompt: What is needed to switch a shift?
options: A supervisor's approval at least 48 hours ahead
questions.explanation: The supervisor must approve it at least forty-eight hours in advance.

questions.prompt: What is true about the cafeteria?
options: It is open 24 hours a day.
It is on the first floor.
questions.explanation: Employees get a twenty percent discount.

questions.prompt: What is not allowed on the production floor?
questions.explanation: 'No jewellery is allowed on the production floor, not even watches.'

questions.prompt: When can Omar join the health benefits plan?
questions.explanation: 'After three months, you'll be able to join our health benefits plan.'

items.title: Getting a library card
items.context: You will hear a conversation between a librarian and a woman who wants a library card.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Hi, I just moved to the city, and I'd like to get a library card.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Welcome! It's free for anyone who lives in the city. I just need a piece of ID with your current address, like a driver's licence or a utility bill.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I have my lease. Will that work?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, a lease is fine. Okay, you're all set. With this card, you can borrow up to fifty items at a time. Books are loaned for three weeks, and DVDs for one week.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: What happens if I'm late returning something?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: We actually stopped charging late fees for books last year. But if an item is more than a month late, we'll charge you the full cost of replacing it, and you won't be able to borrow anything until it's returned or paid for.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Good to know. Can I renew books online?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, through our website or app, up to three times, unless someone else has placed a hold on the book.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I also heard you have language classes.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's right. We have free English conversation circles on Tuesday and Thursday evenings at seven. There's no registration; just show up. You also get free access to an online language-learning program with your card.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Wonderful. And is there somewhere I can print documents?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, at the computers on the second floor. Printing costs ten cents a page in black and white, and fifty cents a page for colour.

questions.prompt: What does the woman need to get a library card?
questions.explanation: She needs ID with her current address; her lease is accepted.

questions.prompt: How long can she borrow DVDs?
What happens if an item is more than a month late?
options: She pays a daily late fee.
She must pay the cost of replacing it.
questions.explanation: The library charges the full cost of replacing it.

questions.prompt: When can she not renew a book?
options: When someone has placed a hold on it
questions.explanation: She can renew up to three times unless someone has placed a hold on it.

questions.prompt: What is true about the conversation circles?
How much does colour printing cost?
questions.explanation: Colour printing costs fifty cents a page.

items.title: Swimming lessons
items.context: You will hear a phone conversation between a parent and an employee at a recreation centre.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Hello, I'm calling about swimming lessons for my son. He's six and has never had lessons before.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Great. For his age and level, he'd start in Level One, Starfish. Classes are thirty minutes long, once a week, for eight weeks.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: What times are available?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: We have Saturday mornings at nine or ten, and Wednesday afternoons at four thirty. The Saturday classes usually fill up fastest.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Wednesday would work best for us, actually. How much is it?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It's ninety-six dollars for the eight weeks, but if you live in the city, it's seventy-two.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: We live in the city. How do I register?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Online registration opens next Monday at seven a.m. You'll need to create a family account first. I'd recommend doing that before Monday, since spots go quickly.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Okay. Does he need to bring anything?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Just a swimsuit, a towel, and goggles if he wants them. Children under seven also need a parent or guardian in the building during the lesson, though not in the water.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's fine, I'll wait in the lobby. Is there parking?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, there's a free lot behind the building. Just make sure to register your licence plate at the front desk, or you might get a ticket.

questions.prompt: Which class time does the father prefer?
How much will the father pay?
questions.explanation: They live in the city, so it costs seventy-two dollars.

questions.prompt: What does the employee recommend doing before Monday?
questions.explanation: She recommends creating a family account before registration opens.

questions.prompt: Why must the father stay in the building during the lesson?
options: It is a rule for all ages.
questions.explanation: Children under seven need a parent or guardian in the building.

questions.prompt: What must he do to avoid a parking ticket?
options: Register his licence plate at the front desk
questions.explanation: He must register his licence plate at the front desk.
